scope: High/medium historical findings after reviewer severity/refutation. Conservative ledger; local implementation does not imply deployment or hardware verification.

findings.title: No request-body limit: anyone can crash the 1 GB fleet host with one large POST, because the whole body is read before login is checked
findings.status: implemented; full CI passed at 38980c0
findings.note: Bound JSON/upload bytes before parsing, including streamed/false-length bodies; total body deadline; actual Caddy configuration validation passed in CI.

findings.title: Nothing limits disk use on the 40 GB fleet disk (deploy DB copies, OTA images, container logs); a full disk breaks the fleet and blocks deploys
findings.status: open; reconcile current code and prior tests
findings.note: Historical finding is not proof the defect remains; no closure inferred here.

findings.title: The drift check says IN SYNC when production runs a commit the local branch does not contain
findings.status: implemented; full CI passed at 38980c0
findings.note: Actual git histories verify that ahead/divergent or dirty deployed identities cannot be called IN SYNC.

findings.title: Room (return) audio is never gated by the PIN session: it keeps going to the last presenter after an admin lock, an idle relock, being superseded, Stop, and even after a reboot
findings.status: owner-deferred
findings.note: Historical owner decision leaves room audio/PIN relationship unchanged.

findings.title: bridge-web has no connection timeout or thread cap: any device on the venue LAN can pin unlimited handler threads and block go-live
findings.status: implemented; full CI passed at 38980c0
findings.note: Sixteen bridge handler slots, ten-second socket timeout and 16 KiB body limit; overload returns 503.

findings.title: 'Diagnose it for me' almost never shows its findings: the bridge cuts command output to 2000 bytes, and the panel parses the cut JSON
findings.status: implemented; targeted tests
findings.note: Complete bounded diagnosis JSON; over-limit report fails explicitly.

findings.title: 'Choppy for them → deepen the bridge buffer' (profile:wan) changes nothing on any bridge; it only restarts media
findings.status: open; reconcile current code and prior tests
findings.note: Historical finding is not proof the defect remains; no closure inferred here.

findings.title: After claiming from the drawer, the Actions tab still says 'Only reads work until this bridge is claimed'
findings.status: open; reconcile current code and prior tests
findings.note: Historical finding is not proof the defect remains; no closure inferred here.

findings.title: Flashed images give user 'pi' the shell /usr/sbin/nologin, so the owner SSH login that 2.2 adds can never open a shell
findings.status: implemented; physical acceptance pending
findings.note: Login shell/password-lock checks; actual new image boot remains required.

findings.title: GStreamer's plugin cache can never be saved on the read-only root, so every pipeline start rescans all 268 plugins, including the return-audio restart at go-live
findings.status: implemented; Pi measurement pending
findings.note: Writable registry cache; no measured Pi startup improvement yet.

findings.title: The CI preflight gate can never fail the build: its exit code is ignored, and its read-only-write check crashes on an unset $ROOT and reports a pass
findings.status: implemented; image build pending
findings.note: Preflight failure propagation and unset variable corrected.

findings.title: The OTA signing key and fleet bootstrap token are repo-wide secrets with no protected environment: any branch's workflow can read them, and a dispatch from any branch can publish a signed release as Latest
findings.status: open; reconcile current code and prior tests
findings.note: Historical finding is not proof the defect remains; no closure inferred here.

findings.title: stage-image.sh cannot find any 2.1 or 2.2 release, and its signature check uses the public key downloaded from the same release (known item h, confirmed)
findings.status: implemented; targeted tests
findings.note: Pinned local key and release identity validation.

findings.title: machine-id is 'uninitialized' on a read-only root, so every boot gets a new random ID and the persistent journal is unreadable across reboots
findings.status: open; reconcile current code and prior tests
findings.note: Historical finding is not proof the defect remains; no closure inferred here.

findings.title: Actions pinned by mutable tags, an unverified moving base image, and a write-scoped token visible to the third-party build step
findings.status: open; reconcile current code and prior tests
findings.note: Historical finding is not proof the defect remains; no closure inferred here.

findings.title: Revert and quarantine silently fail for long-running bash services: umount of a busy bind returns EBUSY, the error is swallowed, and the restart runs the override again
findings.status: implemented; targeted tests
findings.note: Failed detach cannot claim rollback; busy mounts handled through policy.

findings.title: OTA cannot mount the standby slot on the read-only root: /mnt/ota-standby is never created and mkdir fails, after the slot has already been wiped
findings.status: implemented; targeted tests
findings.note: Writable /run mountpoint and failure before formatting.

findings.title: Lifeline guard reverts PROVEN lifeline and agent overrides after any 15-minute stretch without the fleet (it never checks whether the fleet was heard from after install)
findings.status: implemented; targeted tests; full CI pending
findings.note: Proof is tied to exact update bytes and persisted; later outages cannot revert a proven update.

findings.title: Lifeline guard never fires after a reboot without internet: wall-clock arithmetic on a Pi with no RTC and a clock that cannot be saved
findings.status: implemented; targeted tests; full CI pending
findings.note: Boot ID and monotonic uptime bound the unproven trial; future wall-clock timestamps cannot prevent rollback.

findings.title: (e) CONFIRMED: override signatures cover the bytes only, not the name or version, so any previously signed file can be installed under another name or replayed
findings.status: open; reconcile current code and prior tests
findings.note: Historical finding is not proof the defect remains; no closure inferred here.

findings.title: Revoking an owner SSH key through the signed override does not last: revert-script, revert-all, safe mode, or replaying the older signed file all restore it
findings.status: open; reconcile current code and prior tests
findings.note: Historical finding is not proof the defect remains; no closure inferred here.

findings.title: No anti-rollback for whole-OS updates: any validly signed older image, or a manifest for a different product, is accepted
findings.status: partially addressed
findings.note: Wrong-product manifests refused; general anti-rollback policy still open.

findings.title: `--unquarantine` (and the alert's 'Put the parked update back' button) restores EVERY parked version in lexicographic order, so an older, known-bad version can end up installed
findings.status: implemented; targeted tests
findings.note: Newest parked version; cannot overwrite a newer installed override.

findings.title: `revert-all` deletes the pending restarts that its own reverts just queued, so services keep running override code while status reports 'built-in'
findings.status: implemented; targeted tests; full CI pending
findings.note: Revert-all preserves deferred media restarts; actual shell regression verifies no live restart.

findings.title: Loader crash-loop trip counts deliberate restarts, so a healthy media override is quarantined after 3 ordinary restarts in 2 minutes
findings.status: implemented; targeted tests; full CI pending
findings.note: Use systemd automatic-restart history to reset deliberate-start sequences; four manual starts stay installed while real automatic loops quarantine.

findings.title: A trial boot that fails before multi-user.target never rolls back (kernel panic without panic=, or emergency mode, which keeps petting the watchdog)
findings.status: open; reconcile current code and prior tests
findings.note: Historical finding is not proof the defect remains; no closure inferred here.

findings.title: A cross-site GET /api/checks tears down the live mesh helper (the CSRF guard only covers POST)
findings.status: implemented; full CI passed at 38980c0
findings.note: Checks use read-only routes, never rebuilding the live mesh; cross-site checks refused.

findings.title: Signing out during a live session leaves the camera and microphone captured, and the page no longer shows a way to stop them
findings.status: implemented; full CI passed at 38980c0
findings.note: Shared sign-out stops capture before dropping identity; duplicate Studio cleanup removed.

findings.title: The signed update manifest is not bound to a platform or a minimum version: any signed build can be served cross-platform or as a downgrade, and a failed swap is never rolled back
findings.status: partially addressed
findings.note: Platform/protocol/helper binding implemented; complete downgrade policy remains open.

findings.title: After a transport error the app resends the PIN up to three times, so one wrong PIN can lock the bridge for an hour
findings.status: implemented; full CI passed at 38980c0
findings.note: Retry only the read-only protocol probe. Once PIN POST is sent, an ambiguous response returns without automatic retry or helper rebuild.

findings.title: The mesh helper's loopback control proxy (127.0.0.1:18080) lets any web page burn PIN tries under the presenter's mesh identity
findings.status: implemented; Mac/Windows/Linux race tests passed; full CI pending
findings.note: Replace raw TCP forwarding with guarded HTTP. Reject browser metadata, untrusted Host, simple form writes and oversized bodies before mesh dial. Preserve native JSON calls without retrying lost PIN responses.

findings.title: No Host-header check: a DNS-rebinding page can read the app's GET endpoints, including recorded meeting audio
findings.status: implemented; full CI passed at 38980c0
findings.note: All local app GET/POST requests require a loopback Host; DNS-rebinding hostnames rejected before reading recordings or invoking handlers.

findings.title: A page reloaded or reopened during a live session polls with whatever the Bridge dropdown shows, which can switch the live helper to another bridge
findings.status: implemented; browser regression passed; full CI pending
findings.note: Restore live host and bridge identity from engine state; disable source selectors during a session; polling remains read-only.

findings.title: On macOS the start-up orphan sweep misses the GStreamer voice leg, so after a crash the mic stays captured and the next go-live sends a second voice stream
findings.status: open; reconcile current code and prior tests
findings.note: Historical finding is not proof the defect remains; no closure inferred here.

findings.title: A dead or absent local return player makes the page tear down and rebuild the whole session, then show a false 'This app stopped sending' message
findings.status: open; reconcile current code and prior tests
findings.note: Historical finding is not proof the defect remains; no closure inferred here.

findings.title: The bundled ffmpeg (camera/mic capture on every presenter machine) is downloaded unpinned and without a checksum
findings.status: open; reconcile current code and prior tests
findings.note: Historical finding is not proof the defect remains; no closure inferred here.

findings.title: nb's confirmation prompt promises that changes wait until the bridge is idle or the laptop is unplugged. Only deploy does that; reboot and restart act at once.
findings.status: open; reconcile current code and prior tests
